newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians say hotel conceals its Gaza location.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians say hotel conceals its Gaza location.

text.p: Just where is the Days Inn Palm Beach Hotel?
The Internet site for the New Jersey-based motel franchiser describes the hotel as in "Gush Katif, Israel".

But the Palestinian Centre for Human Rights in a statement released on Wednesday accused Days Inn, owned by HFS Inc, of concealing the fact that Gush Katif is a bloc of Jewish settlements in an Israeli-occupied area of the Gaza Strip.
"The Days Inn brochures misrepresent the map of the region. Although the Gaza Strip is internationally recognised as occupied territory, it is not even indicated," said the centre.

A Days Inn brochure contains a map showing the hotel in relation to Tel Aviv and the Israeli port of Ashkelon but does not note the presence of the Palestinian-ruled town of Khan Yunis right next door, much less the Jabalya refugee camp.
Raphael Farber, president of Days Inn Israel, dismissed the charges. "As far as I know, Gush Katif is in the State of Israel," he said, adding that anyone who disagreed was anti-Semitic.
Israel has never annexed any area in the Gaza Strip, captured in the 1967 Middle East war, and the final status of Jewish settlements is to be determined in future peace talks with the Palestinians.
In any case, Farber does not think Israel will be abandoning the hotel. "I don't believe Gush Katif will be returned (to the Palestinians)," he said.

Farber said his company was in talks with Palestinian investors about the possibility of establishing Days Inn hotels in Ramallah or Jericho, West Bank towns under PLO rule in accordance with interim peace deals with Israel.
